newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mostly up, deal slow.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mostly up, deal slow.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mostly higher, with a firmer tone in Tokyo and scattered enquiries for SMR grades aiding sentiment, dealers said.
"A bullish Tokyo market aided domestic sentiment. We feel that local prices will rise further as they expect RSS 1 to reach 300 cents," a dealer said.
June RSS 1 buyer closed a cent up at 281.50 cents ($1.12) a kg and June SMR 20 buyer was steady at Monday's 264.50 cents.
Uncertainty of the raw material situation in Thailand, particularly on RSS 3 rubber has caused other overseas buyers to turn to Indonesia and Malaysia, traders said.
Dealers said the market is expected to hear of more enquiries from European buyers seeking to cover positions ahead of the summer holidays.

"Chinese buyers are a bit quiet this week after enquiring a lot, last here and in Thailand and Indonesia," another dealer said. The South Koreans were also in the market, tendering for latex and sheet for nearby shipment but nothing was transacted, said traders.
Traders quoted SMR CV at 330, SMR L at 308, SMR 10 at 261 and drum latex at 226 to 228 cents for June.
